extraction.name: Prompted Textures Dataset (PTD)
extraction.description: A synthetic texture dataset spanning 246,285 images across 56 texture classes generated via text-to-image models (Stable Diffusion) using artistically-informed descriptive prompts and curated via a three-stage refinement process (frequency filtering, patch variance filtering, and CLIP scoring).
extraction.creator: Blaine Hoak, Patrick McDaniel
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Texture-specific prompts were constructed by combining descriptors across five categories ({Artistic} {Spatial} {Color Enhancer} {Color} {Texture}) yielding 96,768 unique prompts. These prompts were fed into Stable Diffusion pipelines on 12 A100 GPUs to generate 5 unflagged images per prompt, producing 483,840 raw images before refinement.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Up to 60% of initial generated images were flagged by Stable Diffusion's NSFW safety filter despite benign prompts. Flagged images were excluded from the final public dataset for ethical reasons and regenerated until 5 non-flagged images per prompt were obtained.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Synthetically generated images produced using Stable Diffusion pipelines from Hugging Face based on 96,768 combinatorial text prompts spanning 56 texture classes.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A three-stage refinement process was applied: (1) Frequency filtering via Fourier transforms to remove object-like images, retaining the top 80% of images with the highest frequency cutoff threshold (fc) per class; (2) Patch variance filtering dividing images into 50x50 pixel patches to remove the bottom 20% lowest mean patch variance images per class; (3) CLIP score filtering removing the bottom 20% of images with the lowest CLIP scores per class to ensure prompt alignment, resulting in 246,285 final images.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: In addition to prompt-derived semantic class labels, a human evaluation study was conducted with 9 participants evaluating 900 unique images across refinement stages. Evaluators rated each image on a 1 to 5 scale for overall quality and representativeness to the provided descriptor, with optional free-form commentary.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Mean human quality and representativeness scores were evaluated across each refinement step, showing a cumulative 3.4% increase in quality and 4.5% increase in representativeness. Patch variance and CLIP refinement contributed the largest gains to quality and representativeness, respectively.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Enables exploration in interpretability, robustness, and bias analysis in computer vision models. Facilitated the development of Texture Object Association Values (TAV) to reveal model reliance on texture versus shape and understand vulnerabilities to natural adversarial examples.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Performance varied across texture classes: textures common in real objects (e.g., hairy, flaky) achieved higher Inception and lower FID scores, whereas simple, structured textures (e.g., grid, polka-dotted) had worse scores. Additionally, safety filters showed disproportionate sensitivity to specific texture descriptors like 'paisley'. Fourier analysis confirmed the dataset as a whole is not biased toward specific spatial frequencies compared to real texture baselines.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Diffusion models struggle with generating certain structured textures (such as grid and polka-dotted). Descriptors such as 'muted' frequently resulted in lower image quality and lower CLIP scores. The automated NSFW filter exhibits high false positive rates on texture prompts.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Research in computer vision, machine learning interpretability, measuring texture bias in image classifiers, evaluating model robustness, and synthesizing textures.
